# Start here {.unnumbered}

This tutorial teaches how EEG data are analysed in the lab, from the
recording as it comes off the amplifier to the results. It uses a small
piece of real data from one of the lab's experiments.

It is about EEG, not about programming. Every page has working code,
but you are not expected to write any: run it, read what comes out, and
change a number when a **Try it** box suggests one. The code uses the
standard free tools directly (MNE-Python for EEG, with a little NumPy,
pandas and Matplotlib), so what you see here is what you would type
for your own data.

Each chapter with code has an **Open in Colab** button at the top. It
opens a copy of the chapter that you can run and change in your
browser, with nothing to install. You need a Google account.

## The experiment

On each trial a striped disc appeared on the screen. Its stripes varied
in width and in tilt. The participant pressed one of two keys to say
whether it was an "A" or a "B", and was told whether they were right.
Nobody was told the rule; they learned it from the feedback, over five
visits to the lab and thousands of trials. Tasks of this kind are a
standard way to study how people learn categories [@ashby2005]. EEG was recorded from 64
electrodes on the scalp throughout each visit.

## The data

The full dataset is about a terabyte. The tutorial uses a small subset
(about 320 MB):

- six minutes of **raw recording** from one participant's first visit,
  exactly as recorded apart from being stored at a lower sampling rate,
  plus one minute of rest with eyes closed;
- the same participant's **cleaned trials** from all five visits, cut
  around each stimulus, and from the first visit cut around the feedback;
- **average responses** from eleven participants.

All of it is de-identified: participants are `sub-01` to `sub-11`, and
recording dates have been removed.

## The chapters

1. [What EEG measures](chapters/01-what-eeg-measures.qmd): where the signal comes from, what it can and cannot tell you
2. [The raw recording](chapters/02-raw-data.qmd): what is in the file, electrodes, triggers
3. [Cleaning the recording](chapters/03-cleaning.qmd): filtering, referencing, removing blinks, cutting into trials
4. [The brain's response to a stimulus](chapters/04-erps.qmd): averaging, reading an ERP, comparing conditions
5. [Brain rhythms](chapters/05-rhythms.qmd): the power spectrum, alpha, how rhythms change within a trial
6. [Decoding](chapters/06-decoding.qmd): can a classifier tell what the participant saw?
